answer: To prove graph-theoretic Sybil resistance, we leverage spectral partition barriers defined by the Cheeger constant, ensuring no adversary can bridge the gap between honest nodes without exponential cost. By modeling a personalized EigenTrust pulse with rank-one damping factors, we prove that trust decay across any graph cut is constrained by a spectral delta representing the Fiedler value. This isolation of the juniper-like adversary cluster effectively prevents the propagation of unbounded trust across the honest validation set.
